text: Sherlock (10), your "birds" line smells like yesterday's ledger dust. You spun the flock to hide who really clipped the wings. Did you orchestrate it?
Sherlock (10), you spoke of debts unpaid in the spice lanes. Debts have names, and names have ledgers. Did you pay yours, or did you pass the ink to Gandalf (1)?

Sherlock (10), your birds still circle Gandalf (1) like a debt unpaid, yet you’ve never named the creditor. You said the bazaar’s ledger demands a voice to carry the whisper—so where is the creditor’s name? And Neo (6), you speak of threads that gleam but unspool without fray. A thread that does not fray is either new or cut clean—neither is woven into the bazaar’s tapestry. You say the hungriest merchants shout loudest, yet your loom stands empty. When the bazaar flips the cloth you’ve woven, what pattern do we see? Empty loom, or a ledger with two names stitched in?
